title: Monday's boring SaaS, 5 October 2026
dek: 5 October 2026. Ten products this morning, all of them Stripe-verified. The source link is on each note.

companies.name: MaidsnBlack
companies.description: Tech-driven residential and Airbnb cleaning service for DC / Maryland / Virginia. Online "book in 60 seconds" pricing by bedrooms/bathrooms, cleaners in teams of two, weekly / bi-weekly / monthly recurring plans, and a contractor-recruiting portal (mib.moppworks.com) offering scheduling, payments and customer management to cleaners. Founded Feb 2013, US. TrustMRR pricing model: "Contact for Quote".
companies.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 seat subscriptions (per-job billing), ~$105,289 L30, ~$22,872,928 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~10:03 Warsaw (08:03 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Don't run cleaners yourself. Sell the "book in 60s + dispatch + charge after service" stack to one-city cleaning operators (white-label booking widget + contractor payouts), or run the playbook in one metro where nobody does instant online pricing.
companies.whyItPrints: Local service plus thin software, no AI. Recurring cleans become habit revenue, while the booking + dispatch + auto-charge stack lets it run like a marketplace. 13 years of Stripe history adds up to ~$22.9M. Card-on-file, charged after service, is the whole moat.

companies.name: Corsidia
companies.description: Italian course-comparison directory. It picks schools, training bodies and teachers, so users can compare course offers and prices and then contact the organizers directly. Corsidia.org covers publicly funded active-labour-policy training. Free for course seekers. Founded Jan 2018, Italy.
companies.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 seat subscriptions, ~$78,758 L30, ~$3,115,522 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~05:47 Warsaw (03:47 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Build a "compare local course providers" directory for one country/language (PL driving schools, forklift/UDT certs, language schools) and charge providers per lead. SEO pages per city × course type are the product.
companies.whyItPrints: Lead-gen directory for a fragmented, offline-heavy local market (language schools, professional courses, vocational training). Stripe shows $0 seat MRR but ~$79k L30 and ~$3.1M all-time. Since users pay nothing, the money presumably comes from course providers (paid listings or leads). That part is my inference; the founder's description just says "You'll have to figure it out."

companies.name: Tree Nerd Academy
companies.description: Online study platform for the ISA Certified Arborist exam: video lessons, flashcards, glossary, an AI helper. One-time tiers: Starter $60 / Self-Study Protocol $199 / Inner Circle Edition $229. Founded Dec 2025, Sweden.
companies.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 subs (one-time packages), ~$34,423 L30, ~$213,715 all-time, ~95% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~05:21 Warsaw (03:21 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Pick one blue-collar or regulated certification exam with an official body of knowledge (electrician SEP in PL, HVAC F-gas, CDL, NEBOSH, ISA arborist cousins) and sell a one-time prep pack at $60–$230. Pass rates and exam dates do the marketing.
companies.whyItPrints: Certification-exam prep for a trade career, sold to people who need the credential to get paid more. Under 10 months old, with ~$34k L30, ~$214k all-time and a 95% L30 margin. TrustMRR also lists tiny arborist flashcard apps doing a few hundred dollars a month, so the niche has demand and Tree Nerd is clearly winning it.

companies.name: BackPedal
companies.description: London theft-recovery subscription for bikes and e-bikes. Mechanics install covert GSM/GPS/BLE trackers (17 disguised casings), a 24/7 in-house team recovers stolen bikes (company-stated ~80% recovery rate, ~48h typical), and backup theft insurance is underwritten by Sundays (FCA regulated). Annual protection from £153 (~£12.75/mo). Founded Sep 2021, UK.
companies.evidence: ~$25,383 MRR, 372 active subscriptions, ~$59,307 L30 (upfront kit fees + renewals), ~$1,467,646 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~04:13 Warsaw (02:13 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Recovery-as-a-subscription for one high-theft asset in one city (e-bikes in Warsaw, cargo bikes, tools in vans, construction equipment). Partner with a licensed insurer for the backup cover and own the tracking + recovery ops.
companies.whyItPrints: Hardware + ops + insurance wrapper sold as a subscription. Delivery riders and commuters can't afford to lose an e-bike, so they renew. Physical install and recovery ops are a moat no SaaS clone can copy overnight.

companies.name: Evergreen Support
companies.description: Done-for-you customer-support email team for small online sellers / online businesses, billed monthly or weekly ("Start onboarding for $1", free support audit). Founded Jul 2022, US.
companies.evidence: ~$25,100 MRR, 22 active subscriptions, ~$23,175 L30, ~$812,808 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~04:06 Warsaw (02:06 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Productize support for one platform's sellers (Shopify PL, Allegro, Etsy) with fixed weekly pricing plus your own helpdesk tooling. Software is leverage; the retainer is the business.
companies.whyItPrints: Productized service, inbox outsourcing. 22 clients paying ~$1.1k/mo each on average (my calculation from MRR ÷ subs) adds up to ~$25k MRR and ~$813k all-time. Nobody wants to answer "where's my order?" emails, and once a team knows your store's macros, switching is painful.

companies.name: Dotmarket.eu
companies.description: French marketplace for buying / selling digital businesses (SaaS, media, e-commerce, web agencies). Claims 300+ vetted and valued deals a year (company-stated). Registered in Estonia, founded Jan 2020.
companies.evidence: ~$12,903 MRR, 403 active subscriptions, ~$9,043 L30, ~$1,141,337 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~04:05 Warsaw (02:05 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Run a language-local "buy a small online business" marketplace (PL / CZ / DE) with paid buyer access and valuation packs. Local trust and language are the moat versus Acquire.com.
companies.whyItPrints: Deal-flow subscription. Buyers pay recurring access for vetted listings, sellers pay for valuation/listing. 403 subs at ~$32 average (my calculation) is a classic "small ticket × hundreds of logos" print, and French-language focus keeps Flippa/Acquire away.

companies.name: Vacation-rental guest ops
companies.description: Anonymous B2B SaaS that automates guest operations for vacation-rental hosts/managers ("Automate guest operations in your vacation rental for $0/month"). Pricing: €12 / property / month plus a 7% fee on guest upsells. Founded Jun 2023, US. Listed for sale at $600k.
companies.evidence: ~$8,203 MRR, 78 active subscriptions, ~$10,752 L30, ~$218,721 all-time, ~75% L30 profit margin. Asking $600,000. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~07:39 Warsaw (05:39 UTC). No public domain (stealth).
companies.indieAngle: Per-unit pricing + take rate on upsells for one rental vertical (Polish mountain apartments, campsites, boat charters). Hook into the PMS/channel manager they already use.
companies.whyItPrints: Short-term-rental ops glue: check-in instructions, guest messaging, upsells (early check-in, late checkout). Per-property pricing scales with portfolio managers, and the upsell take rate adds GMV-linked revenue. 75% L30 margin.

companies.name: FireCert
companies.description: UK fire & security compliance software for contractors: asset registers built from panel/CSV exports, locked + hashed certificates (BS 5839-1/-6, BS 5266 emergency lighting, BS 5306 extinguishers, PD 6662 intruder, CCTV, access control, dry risers), QR asset tags, visit reminders, client portal, Xero integration. £79/mo Professional, £129/mo Business. Founded Feb 2026, UK. Company-stated 4.9/5 from 47 customers.
companies.evidence: ~$4,515 MRR, 39 active subscriptions, ~$4,542 L30, ~$16,647 all-time, ~95% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~07:06 Warsaw (05:06 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Find one national standard that tradespeople must certify against (PL fire-protection inspections, gas/electrical periodic checks, lift inspections, F-gas logs) and ship certificate generation + asset register + reminders + Xero/accounting sync. SEO on "<standard> certificate template" is the free acquisition channel.
companies.whyItPrints: British Standards paperwork that fire contractors legally must produce and keep, and that has lived in Word templates and spreadsheets until now. ~$4.5k MRR within ~7 months of founding and a 95% margin. This is the Conforme/NDISCompliant shape, but with real money.

companies.name: ImmoWP
companies.description: French "passerelle immobilière": syncs listings from an agency's real-estate software (company-stated 75+ compatible tools, e.g. Hektor, Apimo, Netty, Immofacile, Ubiflow, Whise, SweepBright) into the agency's existing WordPress site. Price, photos, DPE energy labels and "sold" status update several times a day, with failed-import monitoring and a free listings plugin. €500 HT one-time (install + first year), then €150 HT/yr. Company-stated 200+ agencies since 2017. TrustMRR founded date: Sep 2021.
companies.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 subs (one-time + annual invoices), ~$4,629 L30, ~$48,736 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~04:21 Warsaw (02:21 UTC). Note that the all-time Stripe figure is small relative to "200+ agencies since 2017", so some billing likely predates or sits outside this Stripe account (my inference).
companies.indieAngle: Same play for PL real-estate CRMs (Asari, Galactica Virgo, EstiCRM, IMO) → WordPress/Webflow, or for car-dealer DMS → dealer website. Charge setup + annual maintenance; each new supported feed is a new SEO landing page.
companies.whyItPrints: Pure Conductor-lane legacy glue. Agencies already pay for vertical CRMs that export XML/FTP feeds, and WordPress agencies don't want to rebuild sites. Tiny ACV, but integration maintenance is the recurring fee and switching is near-zero churn.

companies.name: Attivita24
companies.description: Italian marketplace to buy and sell small and medium-sized businesses (shops, bars, SMEs) directly owner-to-buyer, without brokers. Listing packages Base €34 / Plus €86 / Premium €149 + VAT. Founded Oct 2025, Italy. Listed for sale at $800k (first listed Feb 2026).
companies.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 subs (one-time listing packs), ~$11,177 L30, ~$88,188 all-time, ~30% L30 profit margin. Asking $800,000. Revenue synced Oct 5, 2026 ~05:28 Warsaw (03:28 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Owner-direct "business for sale" classifieds for one country (PL: sklepy, gastronomia, salony) with paid listing tiers. Pairs naturally with Dotmarket-style valuation packs.
companies.whyItPrints: Classifieds for main-street businesses, an old-school category where brokers charge a lot. Paid listing packs give ~$11k L30 within a year, at a 30% L30 margin (so ad spend is heavy).

honorableMentions.name: easytools / Easycart (Warsaw, PL)
honorableMentions.note: No-code checkout for digital products, courses, subscriptions and tickets on the creator's own Stripe. Transaction fees + plans. TrustMRR shows Stripe-verified GMV ~$2.70M L30 / ~$82.1M all-time. This is creator GMV, not easytools' own revenue. Caveat: Stripe API key expired, and revenue was last synced Nov 21, 2025, so the numbers are stale. Company page states 1.29M transactions / 810k buyers. Third-party EMIS summary: 2025 net sales +77.7% (no absolute figure). Strong Warsaw example of "Stripe-native checkout glue".

honorableMentions.name: TruckerDB
honorableMentions.note: Daily DOT/FMCSA carrier leads + insurance-renewal alerts for dispatchers, insurance agents, compliance agents and factoring companies. All SEO-acquired (founder-stated). Stripe-verified ~$1,878 MRR / 22 subs / ~$2,463 L30 / ~$7,784 all-time, founded Apr 2026. Perfect public-data-glue shape, still small.

honorableMentions.name: PDFBolt (PL)
honorableMentions.note: Privacy-first HTML→PDF generation API (Free / $19 / $79 / $249). Stripe-verified ~$2,154 MRR / 58 subs / ~$2,460 L30 / ~$19.8k all-time. Boring dev plumbing from Poland.

honorableMentions.name: BankPDF (stealth)
honorableMentions.note: Slug suggests a bank-statement PDF tool, but the profile is anonymous with no description. Stripe-verified ~$2,867 MRR / 44 subs / ~$3,860 L30 / ~$67.1k all-time. Accounting-glue shape, details unknown.

honorableMentions.name: Plate Lookup
honorableMentions.note: License-plate / VIN vehicle-history lookup (auction history, recalls, title brands, odometer). Mostly one-time purchases: Stripe-verified ~$7,650 L30 / ~$51.8k all-time ($32 MRR). Public-data resale.

honorableMentions.name: Legal Tech (BG)
honorableMentions.note: Bulgarian legal cloud software (€19 / €49 / €79 per month). Stripe-verified ~$13.4k MRR / 90 subs, but only ~$1.9k L30 / ~$15k all-time. MRR looks like recently annualised or new contracts, so watch before trusting it.
